title: Exploring the Genetic Diversity and Ecological Niche Breadth of Bradyrhizobium in Tropical Ecosystems
content: Bradyrhizobium exhibits exceptional genetic versatility, functional adaptability, and evolutionary resilience, serving as a critical stabilizing agent in tropical ecosystems. However, its full potential remains underexplored, largely because soil health assessments have historically relied on temperate region and studies often analyze traits in isolation rather than tracking genomic responses to combined environmental stresses. This review applies the niche breadth triangle framework to synthesize the genomic structure, evolutionary history, and multi stress tolerance of tropical Bradyrhizobium lineages. We traced the evolutionary trajectory of the strains, detailing how ancestral lineages fist adapted to to acidic, metal rich soils before acquiring mobile symbiosis islands and specialized secretion systems that broaden their host range. In addition, we highlight that tropical lineages harbor an expansive accessory genome of ~39% variable accessory genes, showcasing a significantly more promising adaptive potential than temperate Bradyrhizobium species. Key protective mechanisms reviewed include modified heat shock promoters, robust extracellular matrices, and photosynthetic metabolism, which preserve nitrogenase activity during drought, high temperatures, and flooding. High strain diversity ensures functional redundancy and niche complementarity, maintaining consistent N-fixation under pressure. Consequently, this work demonstrates how local management practices and stress resistant strains can improve rhizosphere conditions that simultaneously building climate resilient agricultural systems.
